identity_anchor: The unique continuous loop geometry combining a musical note and a vinyl record shape.
brand_cues_to_preserve: The specific topological structure of the white line art (note head merging into the staff/record circle).
The rounded, fluid stroke width and terminal shapes.
structure_policy_rationale: Following the 'douyin' and 'alipay' reference patterns: The original logo is a clear, high-contrast geometric symbol. It must be extruded directly into 3D ice without altering the path or topology. The 'red background' must be completely discarded; only the white symbol becomes the ice sculpture, floating on a pure white background.
design_rationale: Netease Music's identity relies entirely on its distinctive logo shape. Following the theme rules, we treat this logo as a physical object made of ice. We strictly preserve the curve continuity to ensure instant recognition, while applying the global 'Ice/Crystal' material rules (translucency, bubbles, refraction) to replace the original flat red/white aesthetic.
must_preserve: The exact curvature and connection point of the music note tail.
The relative size ratio between the note head and the outer ring.
Translucent light blue ice material with subsurface scattering.
Pure white background with soft contact shadow.
can_recompose: The thickness of the icon (extruded to give volume).
Internal texture details (random snowflakes or air bubbles trapped inside the ice).
forbid: Retaining the original red background color.
Opaque plastic or solid blue material (must look like ice).
Flattening the 3D effect (must have Z-axis depth).
Distorting the logo proportions to fit a square block.
generation_direction: Generate a 3D icon of the Netease Music logo (music note inside a circle) sculpted from translucent light blue ice. The object should have a glossy, wet surface with internal air bubbles and snowflake textures. Place it centrally on a clean white background with a soft shadow underneath. No red colors. High-end C4D render style, refraction, subsurface scattering.
